newsitem.title: UK: Clarke - determined to hold firm grip on inflation.
newsitem.headline: Clarke - determined to hold firm grip on inflation.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Wednesday that he was determined to maintain a firm grip on British inflation.
"The economy is performing exceptionally well," he said in a statement after the Bank of England announced a quarter-point increase in interest rates to 6.0 percent.
"We have delivered a combination of healthy growth and sustained low inflation unseen for a generation. I am determined to maintain a firm grip on inflation to sustain this well into the future."
Clarke said his overriding aim was to ensure living standards continue to rise and more jobs are created in the medium term.
"This means we must take no risks with inflation now or in the future," he added.
Recent data meant the government could be confident the pickup in activity it had forecast in the summer was well established.
Revised GDP data showed growth was close to trend in the first half-year and all the indications were that output had accelerated since then.
The housing market was recovering and business surveys confirmed that the pickup in activity was broadly based.
"The strength of activity indicates that a rise in interest rates is desirable if we are to deliver our inflation target of 2.5 percent or less in the medium term," Clarke said.
"Experience has shown that by increasing interest rates early, as I did in in 1994 and I am doing today, possible inflation can be nipped in the bud."
The Chancellor said this was the action of a government prepared to take the right economic decisions to maintain economic recovery for the years ahead.
